The '''2025–26 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team''' represented [[Duke University]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Blue Devils]] were led by fourth-year head coach [[Jon Scheyer]], and played their games at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]], as a member of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]].

The Blue Devils began the season ranked sixth in the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|AP poll]] and won their opening game against [[2025–26 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]] in the Dick Vitale Invitational. They won their next three games before traveling to [[New York City]] to participate in the [[Champions Classic]], where they defeated twenty-fourth ranked [[2025–26 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]. The team won two more games before facing three straight ranked teams. The Blue Devils defeated twenty-second ranked [[2025–26 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]] by nine points in [[United Center|Chicago]] and fifteenth ranked [[2025–26 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] by one point at home in the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]]. They rounded out the run by defeating seventh-ranked [[2025–26 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] by six points in [[East Lansing, Michigan|East Lansing]]. Duke defeated [[2025–26 Lipscomb Bisons men's basketball team|Lipscomb]] before suffering their first loss of the season, by just a point, to nineteenth-ranked [[2025–26 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]]. The Blue Devils had risen to third in the AP poll at the time of the loss and fell back to sixth after it. They began ACC play with ten straight victories. Over the stretch they faced three ranked teams; [[2025–26 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]] was ranked twentieth for both their meetings and twenty-fourth ranked [[2025–26 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]]. Five of the wins were away, and five were at home. The streak included a road trip to California, where the Blue Devils defeated both [[2025–26 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] and [[2025–26 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]]. The team suffered its first ACC lost on February 7, against [[Duke–North Carolina rivalry|rivals]] and fourteenth-ranked [[2025–26 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. After three more victories, including a ranked win over twentieth-ranked [[2025–26 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]], Duke's ACC schedule was broken up by a match-up with top ranked [[2025–26 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]]. The Blue Devils were ranked third at the time, and won 68–63 in the neutral site game in [[Capital One Arena|Washington, D.C.]]. The victory propelled Duke to the top of the AP poll, where they would stay for the remainder of the regular season. They finished ACC play with four straight victories, including a win over eleventh-ranked [[2025–26 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] and a victory in the rivalry re-match against seventeenth ranked North Carolina.

The Blue Devils finished the regular season 29–2 overall and 17–1 in [[2025–26 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish as [[List of Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball regular season champions|regular season champions]], successfully defending their title from the previous year. As the top seed in the [[2026 ACC men's basketball tournament|2026 ACC tournament]], they earned a double-bye into the quarterfinals, where they defeated eight-seed [[2025–26 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] by one point. They advanced over fifth seed Clemson in the semifinals. They successfully defended their tournament title by defeating second seed and tenth-ranked Virginia in the final, 74–70. The Blue Devils earned the ACC's automatic bid to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and were the one-seed, and top overall tournament seed. They were placed in the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#East regional – Washington, D.C.|East region]]. They defeated sixteen-seed [[2025–26 Siena Saints men's basketball team|Siena]] in the first round despite trailing in the second half. They defeated nine-seed [[2025–26 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]] in the second round 81–58 to advance to the Sweet 16. There they defeated five-seed and tenth-ranked [[2025–26 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]] 80–75. Their tournament run ended against second-seed and seventh-ranked [[2025–26 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] in the Elite Eight on a 35 foot shot by UConn with just 0.4 seconds left, completing a 19 point comeback for the Huskies.<ref>{{cite web|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/48342842/uconn-rallies-19-point-deficit-stuns-duke-last-second-3-reach-final-four-men-ncaa-tournament|title=UConn rallies, stuns Duke on last-second 3 to reach Final Four|work=[[ESPN]]|date=March 29, 2026|access-date=March 31, 2026}}</ref> The Blue Devils finished with a final record of 35–3.

== Previous season ==
{{Main|2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team}}

The Blue Devils finished the 2024–25 season {{Win-loss record|w=35|l=4}} and {{Win-loss record|w=19|l=1}} in ACC play to finish in first place. As the first seed in the [[2025 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC Tournament]], held at the [[Spectrum Center]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]], they earned a bye to the quarterfinals and beat [[2024–25 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]], 78–70, to advance to the semifinals. There, they defeated [[2024–25 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]], 74–71 to advance to the championship game, where they defeated [[2024–25 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]], 73–62, to win the tournament championship. The championship was their 23rd conference tournament victory in program history. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament upsets|NCAA tournament]] as the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|No. 1 seed in the East region]]. There, they defeated [[2024–25 Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball team|Mount St. Mary's]], 93–49, in the first round, [[2024–25 Baylor Bears men's basketball team|Baylor]], 89–66, in the second round, [[2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]], 100–93, in the Sweet Sixteen, and [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], 85–65, in the Elite Eight to advance to their first Final Four since the [[2021–22 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2021–22 season]]. In the Final Four, despite leading for nearly the entire game, they ultimately lost to [[2024–25 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]], 70–67, ending their chance at a sixth national championship.

==Season==
The team concluded an undefeated home season, its third of four seasons under [[Jon Scheyer]]. It ended the season with 32 consecutive home wins.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://goduke.com/news/2026/3/7/mens-basketball-no-1-duke-defeats-no-17-north-carolina-76-61-on-senior-night|title=No. 1 Duke Defeats No. 17 North Carolina, 76-61, on Senior Night|accessdate=March 21, 2026|date=March 7, 2026|publisher=[[Duke Blue Devils]]}}</ref>
